newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Bosnian Serb court sentences Moslems to prison.
newsitem.headline: Bosnian Serb court sentences Moslems to prison.

text.p: A Bosnian Serb court passed stiff 20-year prison sentences on Thursday on three Moslem men found guilty of murdering four Serbs last May despite widespread international condemnation of the trial.
The court in the eastern town of Zvornik sentenced four other defendants in the case to one year in prison each for illegal possession of arms.
The "Zvornik seven" surrendered voluntarily last year to NATO peacekeeping troops in Serb-controlled territory and U.S. troops handed them over to Serb authorities.
The men were found near the former Moslem enclave of Srebrenica, the site of a massacre of Moslem men by conquering Bosnian Serb forces in July 1995.

U.N. officials later said Serb police had obtained confessions from the defendants after beating them. The Serb court, ignoring protests from human rights groups, has refused to allow the defendants to be represented by lawyers from Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation and assigned them lawyers.

But the court stopped short of passing the death penalty. "(The Bosnian Serb republic) is one of the signatories of the Dayton agreement and, under Dayton documents, the death penalty is not allowed," presiding judge Petar Stjepanovic said.
